candidates.title: Training LLMs for Multi-Agent Collaboration with Verifiable Information Rewards
candidates.content: Effective collaboration among large language model (LLM) agents in multi-agent systems requires sharing relevant evidence, requesting missing information, and incorporating teammates' contributions into decisions. Training these behaviors is challenging because final task outcomes provide limited feedback on the value of individual messages. We introduce CoSIR (Collaboration via Surprisal-based Information Rewards), a post-training approach that uses a simple, verifiable environment to teach collaboration behaviors that generalize to more complex, unseen tasks. We propose a Bayesian evaluator that scores shared information by its reduction in team surprisal, defined as the sum of the negative log probabilities assigned to the correct option given each agent's available evidence. Requests are scored by the potential reduction in the same quantity if the requested information were truthfully provided. Separate rewards encourage agents to use the received information in their private choices and calculations. candidates.title: Beyond Perfect Teammates: Multi-Agent Collaboration with Unreliable Colleagues
candidates.content: LLM-based multi-agent collaboration is increasingly used to solve complex tasks by dividing work among specialized agents and integrating complementary expertise. Yet existing systems and evaluations largely rest on an implicit perfect-colleague assumption: collaborators provide correct and complete information and respond promptly to requests. In realistic teamwork, however, collaborators may return information that does not answer the intended question, provide insufficient detail to support a decision, or fail to respond to a request. To separate task-solving competence from the ability to recover an unreliable evidence-gathering process, we introduce the Unreliable Colleagues Benchmark (UnCoBench), which organizes behavioral failures through Misaligned, Incomplete, and Missed settings. The main agent need to verify contextual correctness, diagnose information gap and track unresolved dependencies in order to obtain the correct evidence for solving the task. We also introduce a verifiable and scalable automated generation pipeline that pairs LLM-based scenario generation with executable checks of answer uniqueness and role necessity. candidates.title: Who to Trust in Multi-Robot Systems: Joint Robot and Object Hypothesis Trust Inference via Neural-Symbolic Cross-Validation
candidates.content: Multi-robot systems (MRS) offer significant advantages over single-robot platforms by enabling information sharing and coordination for different tasks in complex environments. However, reliable cooperation critically depends on inferring trust over both information sources and their reported hypotheses, particularly under partial observability and potential adversarial interference. Existing approaches frequently depend on pre-established trust relationships or side-channel information, which may not be available or reliable in realistic MRS deployments. This work introduces NeST-Bayes, a neural-symbolic framework that jointly infers robot and hypothesis trust using only inter-robot observation consistency, without requiring preassigned robot trust, reputation information, or side-channel identity signals. NeST-Bayes infers instantaneous trust evidence scores for robots and object hypotheses by reasoning over ego-centric relational graphs constructed from cross-robot observation consistency. candidates.title: AI is mass decompiling games. That's both awesome and scary.
candidates.content: AI is mass decompiling games. That's both awesome and scary. Indie game developer Popcar talks about the recent wave of AI-powered decompilation of existing games, enabling weird mashups between existing games, and producing a boom in game preservation projects to get old games working on new hardware (often in a browser using WebAssembly). I like how this piece captures both the positives and the negatives of this new development: Most people already realized the scary part by now. If AI can decompile games and software, then the entire tech industry is about to explode. Anybody can decompile other software and use it any way they'd like, and nobody can stop them. [...] This is also a big win for preservation. Old games can be ported, modified, enhanced, and made much more easily accessible than before. DAN-ZOSTER is a nationwide randomized study investigating whether vaccination against herpes zoster (shingles) can reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease and dementia in older adults. Herpes zoster is caused by reactivation of the varicella-zoster virus and becomes more common with increasing age. Some observational studies have suggested that vaccination against herpes zoster may also lower the risk of heart attacks, strokes, and dementia, but this has not been confirmed in randomized clinical trials. In this study, approximately 162,000 adults aged 65 years or older living in Denmark will be randomly assigned to either receive the recombinant herpes zoster vaccine (Shingrix®) or receive no vaccine. Participants in the vaccine group will receive two doses given 2-6 months apart. Participants will be identified and invited using Danish national registries and digital mail systems. Information about health outcomes will be collected through nationwide health registries during follow-up. candidates.title: CRISPR-mediated gap-based replacement enables site-specific DNA lesion insertion into long DNA and nucleosomes
candidates.content: Abstract Defined DNA lesions are essential substrates for dissecting DNA repair mechanisms, yet existing approaches remain limited in positional flexibility, lesion diversity, efficiency, or compatibility with long and chromatinized DNA. Here, we present CGRID (CRISPR-mediated Gap-based Replacement for Insertion of DNA damage), a programmable strategy for site-specific installation of DNA lesions into long DNA and nucleosomes. CGRID uses paired Cas9 nickases to generate two adjacent nicks, followed by gap formation and replacement with a synthetic lesion-containing oligonucleotide. This design enables easy and efficient insertion of diverse DNA lesions at user-defined positions without pre-engineered nicking sites or substrate redesign. Applied to long λ-DNA, CGRID supports efficient installation of single lesions and internal double-strand breaks at predefined positions, which are challenging to obtain using existing methods. These molecules enable high-throughput single-molecule analysis of diverse repair pathways including base excision repair (BER), nonhomologous end joining, and microhomology-mediated end joining without hydrodynamic force. candidates.title: Structural basis of assembly-dependent activation of the MAD3–MAD4 nuclease in the Pseudomonas aeruginosa MADS defense system
candidates.content: Abstract The methylation-associated defense system (MADS) is a bacterial antiphage immune system that cooperates with CRISPR–Cas systems to restrict phage infection. Within MADS, the MAD3–MAD4 module has been proposed to function as an ATPase–nuclease module related to the OLD nuclease family, but the molecular basis of its assembly and function remains unknown. Here, we combined cryo-electron microscopy, X-ray crystallography, biochemical assays, and mutagenesis to elucidate the architecture and assembly mechanism of the MAD3–MAD4 complex. We found that MAD3 and MAD4 assemble into a stable 2:2 heterotetramer. Structural and biochemical analyses revealed that MAD3 alone lacks detectable ATPase activity, whereas MAD4 is insoluble when expressed alone. Assembly of the MAD3–MAD4 complex induces a conformational rearrangement in which MAD3 adopts an ATPase-competent dimeric conformation, while MAD4 is stabilized through intersubunit interactions. This heterotetrameric assembly exhibits both ATPase and DNA cleavage activities. candidates.title: HURDLER: a cloning method to overcome length limits in designed repeat proteins
candidates.content: Abstract The number of internal repeat modules remains a major limiting factor in the construction and functional exploration of long repeat proteins. As a solution, we present High-Utility Recursive Directional Ligation for Extended Repeat proteins (HURDLER)—a modular cloning strategy combining codon optimization, seamless insertion of restriction sites, and modified recursive directional ligation. It presents a very robust technique to clone DNA for large repeat proteins, which may also contain non-repetitive parts, with high fidelity requiring a minimal number of individual cloning steps. Using HURDLER, we cloned designed armadillo repeat proteins with up to 85 internal modules, corresponding to >3700 residues. The method also generates intermediate variants with defined numbers of internal repeats, enabling systematic investigation of how the number of modules influences protein structure and function. HURDLER thereby provides a reliable solution to overcome restrictions in the overall number of internal modules used in the construction of very long repeat proteins. candidates.title: PRADA enables in vivo peroxidase proximity labeling for multiomics

candidates.title: Archival data storage using DNA proximity graphs
candidates.content: DNA offers a promising medium for long-term archival data storage, but the high cost of synthesizing data-specific sequences remains a major barrier to its adoption. Here we introduce SPAN (Synthesis-free Proximity-graph Archiving in Nucleic acids), a synthesis-independent storage architecture in which digital information is written as a physical pattern and encoded in the spatial relationships of randomly barcoded DNA molecules. Barcodes are deposited onto a patterned surface, and an enzymatic reaction records pairs of neighboring molecules. Sequencing these pairs produces a proximity graph from which the original information can be reconstructed. We demonstrate this principle experimentally by writing a 136-bit pattern using photolithography and correctly recovering 114 bits. Simulations further establish the physical parameters governing reconstruction accuracy. Our cost analysis shows that the demonstrated system already has lower estimated writing costs than existing DNA synthesis-based methods, and projects a further five-order-of-magnitude reduction using established optical writing technologies. candidates.title: Engineered cells that sense and respond to interleukin-23 with neutralizing therapy for autoimmunity
candidates.content: Engineered cell sensors are powerful tools for monitoring biomarkers and delivering timely therapy. Here we create an engineered cell sensor of interleukin-23 (IL-23), a critical biomarker in many autoimmune diseases, and a therapeutic delivery platform for autoimmune disease management. We utilized Modular Extracellular Sensor Architecture (MESA), a promising platform given its modularity and previously developed cell sensors for immune targets such as IL-10. First, we developed a library of IL-23 MESA receptors by incorporating IL-23-specific nanobody binders and performed high-throughput functional screening. We achieved further receptor optimization by modifying the extracellular linker length and the ratio of receptor chain expression. Receptor performance was highly correlated with predicted geometric features such as binder pair distance and degree of transmembrane domain dimerization. The receptors were limited by poor surface expression and functioned most effectively as sensors for intracellular IL-23. Finally, we modified the IL-23 sensing circuit to output an IL-23 neutralizing nanobody with the potential to reduce inflammation triggered by IL-23 secretion. This sense-a

candidates.title: Programming Targeted Immune Cell Migration Using Orthogonal Chemokine-Receptor Pairs
candidates.content: Chemokines orchestrate the migration of immune cells throughout the body, but harnessing chemokine signaling to engineer targeted cell trafficking is challenging because of their overlapping interactions and broad expression patterns. Here we used structure-guided protein design to engineer orthogonal chemokine-receptor pairs with minimal crosstalk to native systems. T cells engineered with an ortho-receptor selectively infiltrated tissues producing the ortho-chemokine, in vitro and in vivo. By engineering T cells that both sense and secrete the ortho-chemokine, we generated collective swarming behavior in which pioneer cells attract follower cells via an ortho-chemokine gradient self-organized by positive feedback. By providing orthogonal genetic control over both the generation and sensing of chemokine gradients, this system enables the construction of autonomous spatial targeting programs in engineered cells.

candidates.title: Attribute Network-based Ranking (ANeR) identifies conserved translational fingerprints of M-phase
candidates.content: Abstract Entry into M-phase requires mRNA translation, but whether mitotic and meiotic divisions share a conserved translational programme and which newly synthesized proteins promote Cdk1 activation remain unclear. We developed Attribute Network-based Ranking (ANeR), a multi-objective network-based method that ranks mRNAs according to their proximity to a training group across heterogeneous two-condition omics datasets. Applied to 30 datasets covering mitotic and meiotic divisions, ANeR identified a conserved M-phase translational fingerprint. Benchmarking ANeR predictions against independent mitotic datasets, together with experimental validation in Xenopus oocytes, confirmed that ANeR prioritizes proteins whose accumulation increases during both mitotic and meiotic M-phases. Application of ANeR to the meiotic translational programme identified Fam76b and Cdca3 as previously unrecognized translationally activated regulators required for timely Cdk1 activation, demonstrating that ANeR can uncover new regulators of meiotic M-phase. candidates.title: RiboBA: a bias-aware probabilistic framework for robust ORF identification across diverse ribosome profiling protocols
candidates.content: Abstract By mapping ribosome-protected fragments genome-wide, ribosome profiling (Ribo-seq) has uncovered extensive translation beyond conventional coding sequences, revealing non-canonical ORFs (ncORFs) with roles in diverse biological processes. However, robust ncORF identification remains challenging when Ribo-seq datasets exhibit attenuated periodicity. Protocol-induced biases during library construction is an important contributor to this loss, yet most ORF callers do not explicitly model these distortions. Here, we present RiboBA, a bias-aware probabilistic framework for robust ORF identification from Ribo-seq data. RiboBA combines a generative module that jointly infers protocol-induced biases and codon-level ribosome occupancy with a supervised module that identifies translated ORFs and initiation sites from the bias-adjusted profiles. In simulations with known P-site positions, RiboBA improved exact nucleotide- and codon-level P-site assignment relative to a conventional fixed-offset approach. Across simulations and diverse empirical Ribo-seq datasets, together with orthogonal immunopeptidomics evidence, RiboBA accurately recovers protocol-induced parameters and improves n

candidates.title: Substrate energetics in non-templated DNA synthesis by terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase
candidates.content: Abstract DNA polymerases typically use deoxyribonucleoside triphosphates (dNTPs) for DNA synthesis, yet the contribution of the γ-phosphate to catalysis remains unclear. Here, we examine the role of substrate energetics in enzyme-catalyzed polymerization using a fidelity-independent model polymerase, terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase (TdT). Relative to dNTPs, we find that TdT utilizes the canonical deoxyribonucleoside diphosphates (dNDPs) with reduced rates and catalytic efficiencies, but diminished substrate bias. This lower specificity indicates that the γ-phosphate contributes primarily to nucleotide discrimination, rather than phosphodiester bond formation. Furthermore, our work shows that dNDPs and dNTPs with the same nucleobase exhibit comparable activation energies for the rate-limiting step during DNA synthesis, supporting a model in which the γ-phosphate is not required for lowering the energetic barrier for TdT-catalyzed polymerization. These findings define a mechanistic framework for understanding non-templated DNA synthesis and its application in enzymatic DNA synthesis technologies.

candidates.content: Visa, a world leader in digital payments, today announced that Barclaycard Payments has deployed its Unified Checkout solution, enabling its UK merchant customers to unlock seamless payment acceptance and improve ecommerce conversion.

candidates.title: BoA fined $1.2bn over "egregious" AML deficiencies
candidates.content: Bank of America (BoA) has been fined $1.2bn for its "deficient and ineffective" anti-money laundering (AML) process as well as "egregious and continued" violations of the Bank Secrecy Act (BSA).

candidates.title: Businesses view stablecoins warily
candidates.content: Despite the hype surrounding the digital assets, businesses remain cool to using the cryptocurrency, according to the results of a Cleveland Federal Reserve survey.

candidates.title: JPMorgan rounds up partners
candidates.content: The biggest U.S. bank has been collecting payments partners to better integrate software and keep up with industry trends, among other purposes.

candidates.title: Standard Chartered pushes $2T stablecoin forecast to 2030 as transaction volumes grow
candidates.content: The bank identified four distinct stablecoin markets, with USDC leading payments and AI transactions as competition intensifies over reserve yields.

candidates.content: The deal gives Polygon access to 37 money transmitter licenses and 11 state exemptions.

candidates.title: Agent-Guided Evidence Acquisition for Emotion-Cause Pair Extraction
candidates.content: arXiv:2610.14886v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Emotion-Cause Pair Extraction (ECPE) requires identifying the causes associated with emotions expressed in a conversation. Accurate extraction can depend on evidence that is not initially available, making it important to decide when further information is worth acquiring. We study agent-guided evidence acquisition for ECPE, where a student agent selectively accesses expert judgments for borderline relations on both sides of its validation-selected F1 decision boundary and revises only queried predictions. Through controlled comparisons under different information-access conditions, we examine how delegation granularity, query selection, and response integration affect prediction quality. At a nominal 10% query rate, selective fusion improves mean pair F1 by 2.64-3.88 points over the student in our main experiments, reaching 65.14 on ECF and 49.74 on MEC4 across model families. Our analysis suggests that greater access does not always translate into better cause identification. candidates.title: UDHRBench: Benchmarking Human Rights in Large Language Models
candidates.content: arXiv:2610.15179v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models are increasingly deployed in contexts requiring adherence to ethical and legal norms, yet their alignment with internationally recognized human rights standards remains underexplored. We introduce UDHRBench, a large-scale benchmark for operationalising the evaluation of large language model compliance with the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. The dataset comprises 1,124 human rights confronting questions covering all 30 articles and 4,496 responses from four large language models (ChatGPT, Grok, Gemini, and Fanar), manually annotated by experts for alignment, with high inter-annotator agreement ($\kappa = 0.801$). Our analysis reveals systematic and non-trivial misalignments, showing that violations typically arise through seemingly rational reasoning: appeals to efficiency, risk management, or scientific neutrality, rather than explicit rejection of rights. candidates.title: SemTree: Judge-Aware Semantic Decision Trees for Inspectable and Repairable Rule Decisions
candidates.content: arXiv:2610.13999v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rule decisions such as content moderation, advertising compliance, and eligibility checks combine several conditions, exemptions, and missing-information cases, and an error can be fixed only once the failing condition is known. We introduce SemTree, a framework that represents a rule decision as a semantic decision tree: each node is a natural-language question with explicit Yes/No/Unknown criteria, a pluggable semantic judge answers it, and the branching structure is compiled on the answers that this judge actually gives. The executed path is the reasoning behind every decision, so errors are repaired where they occur: a reviewer corrects a single node and replays the rule, corrected nodes become training labels for the judge, and a tool-using LLM editor revises questions and subtrees while observing execution results. candidates.title: Economy of Minds: Emerging Multi-Agent Intelligence with Economic Interactions
candidates.content: arXiv:2606.02859v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: How can a population of agents self-orchestrate and self-adapt into stronger collective intelligence without centralized control? Inspired by Friedrich Hayek's economic theory of decentralized coordination in markets, we study this question through an agent economy in which agents compete via auctions for the right to act, exchange payments, and accumulate wealth from environmental rewards. These simple local incentives induce decentralized credit assignment, driving global planning without explicit orchestration or communication protocols. The population evolves through economic selection: effective agents accumulate wealth and are mutated via exploitation, while ineffective ones go bankrupt and are replaced via exploration. Using modern Large Language Model (LLM) based agents, we show that, initialized with weak agents, the agent economy produces emergent multi-step reasoning strategies and outperforms stronger monolithic baselines across five agentic tasks, including mathematical reasoning, financial research, scientific research, accelerator design, and distributed-system optimization. candidates.title: Every Token Leaves a Ripple in the Stream of Thought: Eliciting Model-Internal Token Saliency for Chain-of-Thought Compression
candidates.content: arXiv:2608.31066v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning improves multi-step problem solving, but long reasoning traces inflate inference cost. Token-level CoT compression reduces this cost by pruning full reasoning chains into shorter traces for model adaptation, making token selection the central challenge. Existing methods often rely on external scorers or heuristic signals only indirectly tied to the model's internal answer computation. We instead adopt a model-internal perspective: as the model forms an answer, each reasoning token induces a ripple in the residual stream whose effect on the answer reflects the token's contribution to the underlying computation. Building on this view, we propose \textsc{MIST} (Model-Internal Saliency for Token-level CoT compression), which defines token importance along two complementary axes: \emph{necessity}, the drop in answer likelihood when a token's internal contribution is removed, and \emph{sufficiency}, the gain in answer likelihood when that contribution alone is provided. candidates.title: AEIOU: A Unified Defense Framework against NSFW Prompts in Text-to-Image Models
candidates.content: arXiv:2412.18123v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: As text-to-image (T2I) models advance and gain widespread adoption, their associated safety concerns are becoming increasingly critical. Malicious users exploit these models to generate Not-Safe-for-Work (NSFW) images using harmful or adversarial prompts, underscoring the need for effective safeguards to ensure the integrity and compliance of model outputs. However, existing detection methods often exhibit low accuracy and inefficiency. In this paper, we propose AEIOU, a defense framework that is adaptable, efficient, interpretable, optimizable, and unified against NSFW prompts in T2I models. AEIOU extracts NSFW features from the hidden states of the model's text encoder, utilizing the separable nature of these features to detect NSFW prompts. The detection process is efficient, requiring minimal inference time. AEIOU also offers real-time interpretation of results and supports optimization through data augmentation techniques. The framework is versatile, accommodating various T2I architectures. candidates.title: Pollard: Governed Semantic Execution Trees for Framework-Independent AI Agent Control and Replay
candidates.content: arXiv:2610.16145v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent frameworks can persist checkpoints, trace tool calls, and limit resource use, but these facilities often assign different identities to execution, governance, and replay. We present Pollard, a framework-independent runtime based on governed semantic execution trees. A step identity commits to canonical input, kind, attempt, and parent identity; the same tree records completion, refusal, resource settlement, and branch history. Strict replay returns a verified stored result without invoking the wrapped operation, while a transactional store coordinates reservations across concurrent workers. Under a signed deterministic freeze, two state-model replicas each executed the evaluation transitions without an invariant violation, retained-lease PostgreSQL groups were tested against exact limits, strict replay avoided external calls, and all semantic mutations were detected with no false alarms on the controls. candidates.title: Audit tools of the trade: Automated Auditor Elicitation Can Be Sensitive to the Context the Auditor Is Given
candidates.content: arXiv:2610.16911v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Does providing additional context to automated AI auditors improve their effectiveness? Using the Petri tool to audit LLM coding agents, we test the impact of providing two types of resources (an external codebase and benchmark transcripts) to LLM auditors, across four auditor-target LLM pairs and three behaviours (harmful compliance, reward hacking, sycophancy). (1) External codebase: We provide the auditor LLM with a fixed, external open source codebase, which prior work finds improves the realism of synthetic audits. Providing this resource suppresses reward hacking in both auditor-target pairs whose baseline rate is above the floor (4.8 to 1.3 and 3.9 to 1.8 on Petri's default 1-10 scale); the remaining two pairs sit at the floor throughout. The suppression recurs in three of four pairs under a different scenario and resource bundle. candidates.title: What Makes a Latent Space Shared? Direct and Recoverable Compatibility in Motion VAEs
candidates.content: arXiv:2610.17376v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A shared latent space is often assumed to make representations from different schemas directly interchangeable, yet sharing parameters, dimensionality, or a prior does not determine how corresponding instances are expressed in latent coordinates. We show that this assumption conflates recoverable correspondence, direct compatibility, and decoder reuse. In a controlled multi-schema motion VAE on HumanML3D, even identical inputs yield only $5.9$--$17.7\%$ raw Recall@1 and $0.221$--$0.484$ paired-token cosine, despite correspondence being almost perfectly recoverable after linear calibration. Cycle consistency strengthens recoverability but still leaves direct retrieval and token agreement near zero. In contrast, only $64$ paired clips raise raw Recall@1 to $88.4$--$90.3\%$ and token cosine to approximately $0.82$, making most post-hoc alignment unnecessary, although crossed decoding remains substantially worse than native reconstruction.
